transcript:
00:00 Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. This is Alex from Redwood, I'm the AE on this pilot, Priya and Jordan from SE are here too. How's everyone doing?
00:07 Marta Lopez: Hi Alex, hi Priya, Jordan. Doing well, thanks. We wanted to focus today on access status and the early perf numbers you sent.
00:15 Alex Chen: Yep, perfect. Quick agenda: access & onboarding, env readiness (VPC/KMS), quick results review, tuning recs, then action items. Sound good?
00:23 Sana Patel: Sounds good. We also have a question about data residency and logs, if we have time.
00:28 Priya Singh: Great. I'll start with the technical access updates. On our side we saw the service account created, but there was a mismatch on the subnet tags so some inference nodes couldn't reach the s3 bucket during the first run.
00:42 Daniel Kim: That was me, I realized the tag name in our terraform was old, pushed a fix yesterday. After that we saw a couple of successful calls.
00:51 Priya Singh: Okay good. Can you confirm VPC peering? We need peering so the private control plane can reach your VPC for metrics.
00:59 Daniel Kim: Peering is partially set; route tables still need the specific 10.3.0.0/16 route added. We'll add those today.
01:07 Alex Chen: Also please add the firewall egress rules we sent in the last email; they're in the pilot-run doc (link: drive/redwood/pilot-plan).
01:18 Eli Turner: On logs, some tokens looked redacted and others not. How is Redwood handling PII in logs?
01:26 Priya Singh: Default is to redact long text snippets in the console but keep structured telemetry like latency and token counts. For private deployments we can toggle retention and push logs to your KMS-backed bucket with customer-managed keys.
01:38 Sana Patel: Good, compliance needs that. Can you share KMS integration steps?
01:42 Alex Chen: Yes, we'll share the KMS integration guide and SOC2 summary after the call.
01:47 Priya Singh: Results update: we ran a small eval set last week. Caveat: the dataset had shorter sequences than your production distribution so latency numbers are optimistic.
01:58 Alex Chen: Priya, walk through the spreadsheet please.
02:02 Priya Singh: In pilot-results.xlsx (drive/redwood/pilot-results.xlsx) there are throughput, 95p latency, and cost per 1k tokens. Baseline median latency around 85 ms per token, 95p ~170 ms on short prompts.
02:21 Marta Lopez: Our prod is closer to 220 ms 95p with typical prompts, so promising but need longer seq run.
02:30 Priya Singh: Agreed. We ran on a pooled shared-hosted node; Dedicated or Private tuning can change numbers. Dedicated tuning of batch size and kernel selection can shave ~20-30% off latency.
02:45 Daniel Kim: Security prefers private deployment (VPC + customer KMS) but we are evaluating cost. Do you have a breakdown?
02:54 Alex Chen: We'll add a cost delta table. Rough rule: Private with dedicated GPU pool is higher Opex but lowers network variance and keeps data in your VPC. Hosted shared is cheaper but multi-tenant variance exists.
03:07 Sana Patel: What is KV cache / prefix caching?
03:12 Priya Singh: KV cache is the key-value cache for transformer attention states; preserving prefix tokens between calls reduces repeated compute and helps latency for related calls. Auto-gen sometimes writes it as K-V cash, apologies.
03:28 Marta Lopez: For chat contexts ~1.2k tokens, is prefix caching helpful?
03:35 Priya Singh: Yes. If you reuse system prompts or long context, caching avoids recompute. For longer contexts we recommend newer kernels which handle attention efficiently; we'll include config snippets.
03:47 Alex Chen: Timeline: when do you need to decide Dedicated vs Private?
03:52 Marta Lopez: Ideally end of month; procurement needs a tentative decision to budget for Q4.
03:58 Alex Chen: Okay, ~3 weeks. We'll prioritize longer perf run and cost/delta table to help decide.
04:07 Daniel Kim: For perf run we need Redwood to use our actual prompt distribution; I can drop a sample payload in the shared bucket.
04:13 Marta Lopez: We'll anonymize any PII before upload.
04:17 Priya Singh: Once we have payload set, we'll run full sequence distribution tests and include quantization and batching profiles.
04:28 Sana Patel: Any concerns about model compatibility with quantization? We heard some models fragile to 4-bit.
04:34 Priya Singh: We'll start conservative: INT8 or 4-bit with GPTQ where supported, validate quality against eval prompts; if quality drops we'll adjust or fallback.
04:46 Alex Chen: From reliability side we have routing fallback policies; if a dedicated node is constrained we can route to a compatible hosted variant automatically to avoid hard failures, though output distribution may vary.
04:58 Marta Lopez: Please surface variants and the policy in the doc.
05:02 Alex Chen: Will add a matrix of model variants + perf/cost expectations in updated spreadsheet.
05:08 Daniel Kim: Network question: is TLS mutual auth required for the private control plane? Our security asked.
05:13 Priya Singh: Private supports mTLS on control plane; data plane can be restricted by IP/VPC. We'll add cipher suites and mTLS details to the KMS guide.
05:23 Sana Patel: Any blockers for the next perf run?
05:27 Daniel Kim: Only the route table entries and final firewall rule; I'll prioritize today.
05:31 Alex Chen: Recap: Alex to share SOC2 and KMS steps and updated spreadsheet; Priya to run long perf tests once payload arrives; Daniel to confirm peering and firewall rules; Marta to finalize success criteria.
05:45 Marta Lopez: One note: the earlier transcript had some words flipped; can you attach raw logs for debugging?
05:51 Priya Singh: We'll include the raw telemetry CSV in the drive, scrubbed for PII according to retention.
05:58 Alex Chen: Wrapping up, thanks everyone.
06:02 Sana Patel: Thanks all.
06:04 Alex Chen: Bye.
